questions.question: SSR vs CSR vs SSG vs ISR — differences, trade-offs, and when to use each?
questions.title: SSR vs CSR vs SSG vs ISR (2026) — Rendering Strategies
questions.direct_answer:
SSR vs CSR vs SSG vs ISR — differences, trade-offs, and when to use each?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the build graph, bundler/runtime split, and deploy path), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** CSR: client renders; SSR: server renders per request; SSG: build-time render; ISR: hybrid with on-demand revalidation; streaming RSC.

**Classic weak answer:** Treating SSR and SSG as the same — SSR is per-request (dynamic), SSG is build-time (static); cache behavior and freshness differ.

**Senior finish:** Map each to use case: marketing site (SSG), authenticated app (CSR/SSR), blog/ecommerce (ISR), real-time dashboards (SSR + streaming).

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **SSR vs CSR vs SSG vs ISR (2026) — Rendering Strategies** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** SSR vs CSR vs SSG vs ISR — differences, trade-offs, and when to use each?

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **CSR: client renders; SSR: server renders per request; SSG: build-time render; ISR: hybrid with on-demand revalidation; streaming RSC**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Treating SSR and SSG as the same — SSR is per-request (dynamic), SSG is build-time (static); cache behavior and freshness differ**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Map each to use case: marketing site (SSG), authenticated app (CSR/SSR), blog/ecommerce (ISR), real-time dashboards (SSR + streaming)**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** CSR: client renders; SSR: server renders per request; SSG: build-time render; ISR: hybrid with on-demand revalidation; streaming RSC
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

sections.title: Mental model (flowchart)
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart TB
    REQ[Incoming request] --> EDGE[CDN / reverse proxy]
    EDGE -->|static assets| OBJ[(Object store / CDN)]
    EDGE -->|HTML / SSR| SSR[Node or edge SSR]
    SSR --> RSC[Render + data fetch]
    RSC --> CACHE[Set cache-control / surrogate keys]
    CACHE --> RESP[Response to browser]
    RESP --> HYDR[Client hydrate / islands]
```

sections.title: Answer scaffold (what to cover vs what to avoid)
sections.content:
| Angle | What a strong answer includes |
|---|---|
| **What interviewers probe** | CSR: client renders; SSR: server renders per request; SSG: build-time render; ISR: hybrid with on-demand revalidation; streaming RSC |
| **Weak signal (avoid)** | Treating SSR and SSG as the same — SSR is per-request (dynamic), SSG is build-time (static); cache behavior and freshness differ |
| **Differentiator** | Map each to use case: marketing site (SSG), authenticated app (CSR/SSR), blog/ecommerce (ISR), real-time dashboards (SSR + streaming) |
| **Proof you shipped it** | Metrics (LCP, error rate), tests, DevTools trace, or incident story |

sections.title: Trade-offs & senior signal
sections.content:
### Trade-offs interviewers expect you to name

- **Speed vs safety** (types, runtime checks, validation).
- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.
- **Strong answer:** names **treating SSR and SSG as the same — SSR is per-request (dynamic), SSG is build-time (static); cache behavior and freshness differ** and what you do instead.

sections.title: Key points (memorize this list)
sections.content:
- **Headline definition** in one sentence.
- **Mechanism:** CSR: client renders; SSR: server renders per request; SSG: build-time render; ISR: hybrid with on-demand revalidation; streaming RSC
- **Pitfall:** Treating SSR and SSG as the same — SSR is per-request (dynamic), SSG is build-time (static); cache behavior and freshness differ
- **Differentiator:** Map each to use case: marketing site (SSG), authenticated app (CSR/SSR), blog/ecommerce (ISR), real-time dashboards (SSR + streaming)
- **Proof:** DevTools / Network / Performance trace, test strategy, or metric.
- **Close:** decision rule + sensible follow-up question back to the interviewer.

sections.title: How to answer verbally (timed)
sections.content:
**Open (15–20 seconds):** Restate the question and give the one-sentence definition.

**Body (45–60 seconds):** Walk through **CSR: client renders; SSR: server renders per request; SSG: build-time render; ISR: hybrid with on-demand revalidation; streaming RSC** as a story: what runs, what breaks, what you log/measure.

**Pitfall (15 seconds):** Call out **Treating SSR and SSG as the same — SSR is per-request (dynamic), SSG is build-time (static); cache behavior and freshness differ** — interviewers reward honesty about real bugs.

**Finish (15–20 seconds):** Add **Map each to use case: marketing site (SSG), authenticated app (CSR/SSR), blog/ecommerce (ISR), real-time dashboards (SSR + streaming)**, then offer a trade-off question back (“do you optimize for TTFB or TTI here?”).
